title: Debt remediation: active-plan statuses, root lock ignore, Windows CI evidence
objective: Remove the open debt found in Sprints 1-2: active-plan updates leave coherent phase statuses, the root state-writer lock is ignored by git per ADR-0002, and the Windows CI evidence for the new checks is recorded.

phases.title: Debt fixes
phases.objective: Fix debt-1 and debt-2 with regression coverage.

tasks.title: Keep phase statuses coherent after plan --update-active (debt-1)
tasks.description: kyro plan --update-active left phase statuses incoherent (P1 'active', P2/P3 'blocked' while every task was pending), producing kyro analyze coherence findings until kyro repair normalized them. Make the active-plan update derive phase and sprint statuses exactly as repair/analyze expect, for every task-state combination it can produce.
tasks.context: debt-1. Observed 2026-10-30 rewording T1.1 criteria in this scope; kyro repair (src/cli/commands/repair.ts) normalizes phase/sprint statuses from task states, and kyro analyze flags mismatches as coherence findings. Implementation is delegated to Sol 6.1; QA by Astra. Requirement and scenario links are added by the orchestrator right after planning.
acceptance_criteria: After plan --update-active on a sprint whose tasks are all pending, every phase status is pending and kyro analyze reports no coherence finding — proven by npm run check:active-plan.
After an update on a sprint with mixed task states (done, pending with unmet dependencies, ready), phase statuses equal what kyro repair would derive — proven by the same check.
npm run build and npm run check:active-plan pass.

evidence.summary: Implemented by Sol 6.1. Root cause: update-active passed execution states (ready/blocked) to derivePhaseStatus, so a phase with a ready pending task became 'active' and one waiting on dependencies 'blocked', while repair/analyze derive persisted statuses from task statuses only. active-plan.ts now uses the same derivation as repair/analyze.
validation: npm run check:active-plan: pass — 'ok all-pending update uses repair/analyze status derivation', 'ok mixed done/pending/ready update uses repair/analyze status derivation' (also checks analyze coherence and that a following repair changes nothing); '18 active-edit, freshness and immutable-history groups passed' (reported by Sol 6.1, outside sandbox)
npm run build: pass (reported by Sol 6.1)
Live reproduction in this scope (orchestrator): update-active on Sprint 3 produced P1 active / P2 blocked with all tasks pending before the fix

checked_criteria: After plan --update-active on a sprint whose tasks are all pending, every phase status is pending and kyro analyze reports no coherence finding — proven by npm run check:active-plan.
After an update on a sprint with mixed task states (done, pending with unmet dependencies, ready), phase statuses equal what kyro repair would derive — proven by the same check.
npm run build and npm run check:active-plan pass.

tasks.title: Ignore the root state-writer lock via the local git exclude file (debt-2, ADR-0002)
tasks.description: Implement ADR-0002: install and sync idempotently add '/.kyro-state-writer.lock*' (prefixed with the workspace path when the Kyro workspace is a repository subdirectory) to the repository's local exclude file resolved with git rev-parse --git-path info/exclude; never write the root .gitignore or any tracked file; outside git write nothing. kyro doctor WARNs with the exact remedy when the root lock path is not ignored.
tasks.context: debt-2, ADR-0002. Lock name: STATE_WRITER_LOCK exported from src/cli/pipeline/state-writer-lock.ts (root .kyro-state-writer.lock/ plus .kyro-state-writer.lock.reclaim-* leftovers). Existing ignore helpers and doctor diagnostics live in src/cli/core/git-trackability.ts. Global rule git-exclude-kyro-lock applies. Implementation delegated to Sol 6.1; QA by Astra.
acceptance_criteria: In a temp git repo, install and sync add exactly one exclude entry for the root lock (idempotent across repeated runs) and a held lock directory plus a reclaim leftover do not appear in git status --porcelain — proven by npm run check:git-trackability.
With the workspace in a repository subdirectory the entry is prefixed and effective; outside git nothing is written; no tracked file changes — proven by the same check.

kyro doctor WARNs with a remedy when the root lock path is not ignored and passes after install — proven by the same check; npm run build, npm run check:install-rehydrate, and npm run check:update pass.

evidence.summary: Remediation of Astra findings by Sol 6.1 (T3.1 unchanged). git-trackability.ts now validates the exclude destination against the git dir and common dir, rejects symlinks in info/ and exclude, opens without following links and verifies descriptor identity before writing (M1); rejects workspace prefixes with control characters or line separators and omits unsafe exact-line remedies (M2); distinguishes confirmed non-repository from failed git discovery and WARNs with a PATH remedy (m1); bounds git subprocesses to 10 s. Original ADR-0002 behavior retained: idempotent local exclude entry from install/sync, prefixed for subdirectory workspaces, nothing outside git, doctor WARN/PASS.
validation: npm run check:git-trackability: pass — 'ok M1 symlinked exclude: tracked target byte-identical; install/sync nonfatal; doctor WARN'; 'ok M2 line-separator workspace paths: exclude byte-identical; unrelated secret.txt visible; unsupported workspace path WARN'; 'ok m1 unavailable Git: discovery WARN with PATH remedy; no writes'; 'ok Git calls use 10 s timeout; timed-out discovery WARNs and stays nonfatal'; original root/nested/worktree/outside-git/doctor cases pass (reported by Sol 6.1, outside sandbox)
npm run build, check:install-rehydrate, check:update: pass (reported by Sol 6.1)
evidence.notes: Native Windows execution not verified locally; the portable identity fallback was simulated. Windows CI runs on the next push.

checked_criteria: In a temp git repo, install and sync add exactly one exclude entry for the root lock (idempotent across repeated runs) and a held lock directory plus a reclaim leftover do not appear in git status --porcelain — proven by npm run check:git-trackability.
With the workspace in a repository subdirectory the entry is prefixed and effective; outside git nothing is written; no tracked file changes — proven by the same check.

kyro doctor WARNs with a remedy when the root lock path is not ignored and passes after install — proven by the same check; npm run build, npm run check:install-rehydrate, and npm run check:update pass.
